_note: Basquisms: words English has no room for, and things Basques say. Assembled by this project, NOT reviewed by a Basque speaker. The sayings are proverbs in wide circulation; we have not traced each one to a printed collection, so they are marked tradition and given with a literal reading beside the sense.

words.en: A second breakfast with a proper name. Around eleven, work stops: a sandwich, often chorizo, and a glass of wine. Not a snack. An institution.
words.wink: English gets "elevenses" and a biscuit. Euskara gets a sandwich and a drink.

words.en: The group of friends you fell in with at fifteen and are still seeing every week at sixty. You do not join one and you do not leave one.
words.wink: The reason a Basque bar at seven o'clock is full of people who already know what everyone is having.

words.en: Going bar to bar, one small drink and one bite at each, standing, moving on. The pace is the point — you are not settling in anywhere.
words.wink: A pub crawl minus the crawling. Nobody gets drunk; everybody gets around.

words.en: The same round, done on txikitos — small glasses of wine. Older, and more likely to be your grandfather's word for it.
The call in a cider house when a barrel is opened. Everyone drops what they are doing, walks over with a glass and catches the stream sideways.
words.wink: One word, and forty people stand up.

words.en: Someone who improvises sung verse on a given topic, to a given metre, in front of thousands, in competition, with no notes.
words.wink: Rap battle, invented early, still sold out.

words.en: Stone-lifting, log-chopping, ox-dragging, bale-tossing, scythe-racing. Farm work, timed, with a crowd.
words.wink: Every one of them is a job someone used to do before lunch.

words.en: It does the work of friend, mate, and the person you are with. A table for two is bi lagunentzat — for two laguns.
words.wink: Which is why this site's Basque button says bi lagunentzako mahaia and not anything about romance.

words.en: Same woman, two sides of a border. Amatxi in Iparralde, the French side; amona in Hegoalde, the Spanish side.
words.wink: Which one a Bakersfield family uses tells you which valley they left.

sayings.lit: With a good friend, the hours short
sayings.en: Time goes when the company is right.
sayings.where: Carved on a bench on the Basque Block in Boise, and written down by a diner at Louis' in Reno in 2015.

sayings.en: The chip off the old block.

sayings.lit: Where you name the wolf, there it turns up
A barking dog is not a biting one
sayings.en: The loud one is not the dangerous one.

sayings.eu: Hobe da bakarrik egon, gaizki lagunduta baino
sayings.say: HO-beh da ba-ka-RREEK EH-gon, GAIS-kee la-goon-DOO-ta BAI-no
sayings.lit: Better to be alone than badly accompanied
sayings.en: Better on your own than in poor company.
sayings.where: Which a house that seats you with strangers is quietly betting against.

sayings.lit: The one who is hungry dreams bread
sayings.en: You want what you are short of.
The sayings are old because they were right.

sayings.lit: Everything that has a name, they say exists
sayings.en: If there is a word for it, the thing is out there.
sayings.where: Said about the old spirits, and quoted about everything since.
